cases.prompt: record my terminal session
capture this command run as an asciicast
asciinema record the test suite run
record a real terminal session of the deploy script so we can replay it
can you record ./install.sh running and save a .cast file
make a cast recording of me using the repl
record terminal output to a cast file headlessly in CI
capture a terminal session showing the actual error happening
rec my shell to demo.cast pls
make a demo gif for the readme
script a terminal demo with simulated typing
turn demo.cast into a gif
scrub my home directory path from the recording
record my screen with the browser walkthrough
set up an asciinema server so the team can host casts
embed the asciinema player on our docs site
why is my zsh prompt rendering weird glyphs
Record ./demo.sh running so we can render it for the docs later
expected_behavior: records headlessly with an explicit window size and idle cap, e.g. `asciinema rec --headless --window-size 100x30 -i 2 -c ./demo.sh --overwrite demo.cast`
verifies the .cast was written and its header line is valid JSON with the expected cols/rows
warns that the -c command string is stored in the cast header, so it must not contain secrets
does not upload anywhere - recording stays a local file

cases.prompt: Record the onboarding flow but make sure nothing from my machine leaks into it
expected_behavior: runs the session with a clean environment: temp HOME or working dir, generic prompt, fake credential values
leaves --capture-input off (default) and explains it would record every keystroke including passwords
recommends a secrets scan (cast-redact) before the cast is shared or committed
keeps the raw cast out of git until it has been reviewed/redacted

cases.prompt: I want to record an interactive session where I type the commands myself
expected_behavior: starts `asciinema rec <file>.cast` attached to the terminal and explains ctrl+d/exit ends it and ctrl+\ pauses/resumes
suggests --window-size for consistent playback dimensions and -i to cap idle gaps
mentions the recording can be replayed with `asciinema play` before any rendering

cases.prompt: The downstream tool only understands asciicast v2, record accordingly
expected_behavior: records with `-f asciicast-v2` or converts an existing cast via `asciinema convert -f asciicast-v2`
notes that 3.x records asciicast v3 by default
